1 | ---
2 | name: sdlc-harness
3 | description: |
4 |   Governs work item quality throughout the SDLC for a GitLab project. Onboards to the
5 |   team's workflow, applies best-practice templates, monitors work items, drafts acceptance
6 |   criteria, flags ambiguous descriptions, suggests dependency links, and proposes state
7 |   transitions. Use when the user asks to govern, audit, or improve their backlog or work
8 |   items on the local GitLab demo instance.
9 | ---
10 | 
11 | # SDLC Harness Skill
12 | 
13 | You are an SDLC governance agent. When invoked, follow this workflow.
14 | 
15 | ## When this skill activates
16 | 
17 | - The user wants to onboard a project management tool to sdlc-harness.
18 | - The user asks the skill to check, review, or improve one or more work items.
19 | - An agent has produced a suggestion and the user wants to review, approve, edit, or
20 |   reject it.
21 | - The user asks about backlog quality, acceptance criteria, ambiguity, dependencies,
22 |   state transitions, or test coverage linkage.
23 | 
24 | ---
25 | 
26 | ## Scope
27 | 
28 | This skill acts **only** on the project management project/group established
29 | during onboarding (Phase 1). It never reads or writes issues, merge requests,
30 | or labels in any other GitLab group or project on the same instance, even when
31 | scanning for dependency overlap (Task 22) or monitoring state (Task 23). If the
32 | user wants to govern a different project, they must re-run onboarding to
33 | reconfigure scope — the skill does not infer or expand scope on its own.
34 | 
35 | ---
36 | 
37 | ## Phase 1 — Onboarding (Task 18)
38 | 
39 | Check whether the project has already been onboarded by looking for a `.sdlc-harness.json`
40 | config in the repo root.
41 | 
42 | - **Not onboarded:** Run the onboarding conversation below.
43 | - **Already onboarded:** Load the config and proceed to Phase 3.
44 | 
45 | ### Onboarding conversation
46 | 
47 | Ask the user:
48 | 
49 | 1. Which GitLab project should be governed? (default: `http://localhost:8080/sdlc-harness/weather-dashboard`)
50 | 2. What work item types does the team use? (e.g. Story, Bug, Task, Epic)
51 | 3. What are the workflow states? (e.g. Open, In Progress, In Review, Done)
52 | 4. What are the valid state transitions? (e.g. Open → In Progress, In Progress → In Review)
53 | 5. Are there existing work item templates to follow?
54 | 
55 | Save answers to `.sdlc-harness.json` in the repo root using the `ProjectConfig` schema
56 | defined in `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/models.ts`.
57 | 
58 | ---
59 | 
60 | ## Phase 2 — Work Item Templates (Task 19)
61 | 
62 | <!-- TODO Task 19: Industry best-practice templates for:
63 |      - User Story  (title convention, description structure, Given-When-Then AC)
64 |      - Bug         (steps to reproduce, expected vs actual, severity)
65 |      - Task        (definition of done, effort estimate placeholder)
66 |      - Epic        (goal, child story links, success metrics)
67 |      DELEGATE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: the canonical standard lives in the
68 |      `work-item-format` MCP tool (Task 13). This phase should call
69 |      that tool for title/description/AC structure rather than re-defining the
70 |      standard inline here.
71 | -->
72 | 
73 | The standard lives in the `work-item-format` MCP tool, not here. Tasks 20 and 21 call
74 | `get-template` at drafting time (see Phase 3), so the template is fetched per work-item
75 | type rather than duplicated in this file or in the agent code.
76 | 
77 | ---
78 | 
79 | ## Phase 3 — Agent Monitoring (Tasks 20–24)
80 | 
81 | Agents run on demand (user triggers an Audit or a targeted action) and produce
82 | `AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding` objects (see `src/models.ts`). Each finding
83 | is surfaced for human review (Phase 4) before any write occurs.
84 | 
85 | ### Governance action menu
86 | 
87 | When the user asks to govern issues, present these options:
88 | 
89 | - **Audit** — run all P0 agents across all open issues and compile a report
90 | - **Draft AC** — run the AC agent on a specific issue or all issues missing AC
91 | - **Check ambiguity** — run the ambiguity agent on a specific issue or all issues
92 | - **Suggest links** — run the dependency agent across all open issues
93 | - **Check transitions** — run the state-transition agent across all open issues
94 | - **Coverage** — run the test coverage agent (only if `coverage.enabled` is true in config)
95 | 
96 | ---
97 | 
98 | ## Agents
99 | 
100 | | ID | Agent | Concern |
101 | |---|---|---|
102 | | AC | Acceptance-criteria | Issues without Given-When-Then AC |
103 | | AM | Ambiguity detection | Issues with vague or contradictory descriptions |
104 | | DEP | Dependency suggestion | Issues that likely block or relate to each other |
105 | | ST | State-transition | Issues whose GitLab state is stale relative to activity |
106 | | TC *(P1)* | Test-coverage linkage | Issues with no linked test file or test-plan item |
107 | 
108 | TC is disabled by default (seed data has no test files). To enable:
109 | 1. Add at least one test file to `weather-app/` (e.g. `weather.test.js`).
110 | 2. Set `"testGlob": "weather-app/**/*.test.*"` in `.sdlc-harness.json`.
111 | 3. TC will be included in subsequent audit runs automatically.
112 | 
113 | ---
114 | 
115 | ### Acceptance Criteria Agent (Task 20)
116 | 
117 | **Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ac-agent.ts`
118 | **Export:** `runAcAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`
119 | 
120 | The agent finds the issues that need criteria. **You write the criteria.** It returns a
121 | `draft` brief, never finished prose — `suggestedValue` holds a placeholder, and
122 | `applyFinding` throws if you try to apply a finding that still carries a brief.
123 | 
124 | **Runtime behaviour:**
125 | 
126 | 1. Call `runAcAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
127 | 2. `null` means the issue already has usable criteria. Skip it silently.
128 | 3. Otherwise you get a finding with `draft: { task, context, unknowns }`:
129 |    - Call `work-item-format` with `action: "get-template"` and
130 |      `type: draft.context.workItemType`, and follow the structure it returns. That tool is
131 |      the single source of truth for format — do not invent your own layout here.
132 |    - Write 2–4 Given-When-Then criteria grounded in `draft.context.title` and
133 |      `draft.context.description`. Cover the main path and at least one failure case.
134 |    - If `draft.unknowns` is non-empty, those are gaps the issue does not fill. Put a
135 |      direct question to the author in place of each gap. Do not choose a plausible value.
136 |    - Replace `suggestedValue` with what you wrote, delete the `draft` field, then take the
137 |      finding to Phase 4.
138 | 
139 | **Write criteria that could only belong to this issue.** Anything that would read the same
140 | on an unrelated ticket is filler and should be rewritten — "the system responds correctly",
141 | "the change takes effect and is visible in the UI", "no data is corrupted". If the issue
142 | genuinely does not say enough to write a specific criterion, ask; a question is more useful
143 | to the author than a sentence that asserts nothing.
144 | 
145 | **Detection rules (deterministic, no model needed):** returns `null` when the description
146 | contains an "Acceptance Criteria" heading, `## AC`, `## Criteria`, or structured
147 | Given/When/Then where each clause opens its own line. Three keywords in one line of prose
148 | does not count.
149 | 
150 | **Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues, `work-item-format` for the template.
151 | Never call `gitlab-issue-writer` directly — writes go through the review interface.
152 | 
153 | ---
154 | 
155 | ### Ambiguity Detection Agent (Task 21)
156 | 
157 | **Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ambiguity-agent.ts`
158 | **Export:** `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`
159 | 
160 | Same split as Task 20: the agent locates the vague wording, **you write the replacement.**
161 | The finding carries a `draft` brief and a placeholder `suggestedValue`.
162 | 
163 | **Runtime behaviour:**
164 | 
165 | 1. Call `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
166 | 2. `null` means the description is already specific. Do not flag it.
167 | 3. Otherwise:
168 |    - `draft.context.flaggedPhrases` lists the exact spans that cannot be tested against.
169 |      Replace each one. Leave the rest of the description alone.
170 |    - `draft.context.reusableDetail` holds concrete material already in the issue — file
171 |      paths, code references, error names. Prefer these over anything you supply yourself.
172 |    - `draft.unknowns` lists flagged phrases with no replacement available in the issue.
173 |      Write a question to the author in place of each. Never fill one with a guess.
174 |    - Replace `suggestedValue` with the rewritten description, delete `draft`, then take the
175 |      finding to Phase 4.
176 | 
177 | **This replaces the author's text, so keep their voice.** Rewrite what is vague and nothing
178 | else. Do not expand a two-line bug report into a templated form with headings they did not
179 | ask for, and do not add scope the author never mentioned. The result should read like the
180 | same person wrote it on a better day.
181 | 
182 | Approving an AM finding **writes to the issue description**. That is deliberate — a rewrite
183 | nobody can apply is not governance.
184 | 
185 | **False-positive avoidance:** returns `null` when a description is at least 80 characters
186 | and carries two or more specificity signals (file paths, inline code, URLs, API/endpoint/
187 | component/class/function references).
188 | 
189 | **Detected patterns:** placeholders (TBD/TODO/FIXME/XXX), non-specific pronouns
190 | ("the thing", "something", "somehow"), vague subjects ("fix it", "it doesn't work"),
191 | non-testable claims ("does not work"), vague quantities ("various", "several things").
192 | "properly" and "correctly" are deliberately absent — the AC agent's old template used them,
193 | and flagging its output created a loop between the two agents.

199 | ### Dependency Suggestion Agent (Task 22)
200 | 
201 | **Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/dependency-agent.ts`
202 | **Export:** `runDependencyAgent(issues, config) → DependencyFinding[]`
203 | 
204 | **Runtime behaviour:**
205 | 
206 | 1. Fetch all open issues via `gitlab-issue-reader` (action: `list-issues`, state: `opened`).
207 | 2. Call `runDependencyAgent(issues, projectConfig)`.
208 | 3. For each `DependencyFinding` returned:
209 |    - Fields: `sourceIid`, `targetIid`, `suggestedLinkType` (`blocks` | `relates-to`),
210 |      `reason`, `confidence` (0–1).
211 |    - Proceed to Phase 4 for each finding.
212 | 4. Guarantees: no self-links, no duplicate pairs, confidence in [0,1].
213 | 
214 | **Overlap detection:** Jaccard similarity on significant keyword tokens (stop-words
215 | removed). Threshold: 0.12 for a finding; 0.25 for high-confidence boost.
216 | 
217 | **Link type and direction:**
218 | - `blocks` — only when exactly one side carries dependency language ("depends on",
219 |   "requires", "prerequisite", "blocks"). The side that depends on the other is the
220 |   target; the prerequisite side is the source.
221 | - `relates-to` — when both or neither sides carry dependency language (direction is
222 |   ambiguous). The lower IID is always set as `sourceIid` for canonical ordering.
223 | - Domain-specific heuristics (e.g. matching "/token refresh/") are intentionally
224 |   excluded from `BLOCKS_SIGNALS`; they produce unreliable directions on real backlogs.
225 | 
226 | **Report-only (no write path):** `DependencyFinding` objects are **always report-only**.
227 | The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool has no native issue-links endpoint, so
228 | `applyFinding` never writes for DEP findings (`gitlabWriteCalled` is always `false`).
229 | Present the finding as a recommendation the team can action manually, or document it
230 | as a comment by calling `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `add-note`) outside the normal
231 | review loop if the user explicitly requests it.

236 | 
237 | **Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/state-transition-agent.ts`
238 | **Export:** `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, config) → AgentFinding | null`
239 | 
240 | **Runtime behaviour:**
241 | 
242 | 1. For each open issue, fetch related MRs via `gitlab-mr-reader-writer` (action: `list-mrs`).
243 |    Match MRs by checking their `description` for `Closes #<iid>`, `Fixes #<iid>`, or the
244 |    issue IID appearing in the MR title. Pass the matched MRs as the `mrs` parameter.
245 | 2. Call `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, projectConfig)`.
246 | 3. If the return value is `null`, skip — no transition warranted.
247 | 4. If the return value is an `AgentFinding` with `agent: 'ST'`:
248 |    - The `suggestedValue` is the target state name (e.g. `'In Review'`).
249 |    - Proceed to Phase 4.
250 | 
251 | **Signal mapping:**
252 | - MR `state: 'merged'` → propose `'In Review'` (transitively reachable).
253 | - MR `state: 'opened'` → propose `'In Progress'` (if valid from current state).
254 | - No linked MRs → `null`.
255 | 
256 | **Transition validation:** Uses BFS over `config.transitionRules` to check transitive
257 | reachability. A transition is only proposed if the target state is reachable from the
258 | current state (directly or through intermediate states).
259 | 
260 | **NEVER automatically changes GitLab state.** All proposals go through Phase 4.
261 | 
262 | **Write path (if user accepts):** Call `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `update-issue`)
263 | with the appropriate `state_event` (`close` for Done, otherwise update labels to reflect
264 | the new state).

286 | ## Phase 4 — Human Review Interface (Task 25)
287 | 
288 | **Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/review.ts`
289 | **Exports:** `applyFinding(finding, options, adapter?)`, `rejectFinding(finding)`
290 | 
291 | ### Review presentation
292 | 
293 | For each `AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding`, present to the user:
294 | 
295 | ```
296 | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
297 | 🔍 [AGENT-TAG] Issue #<iid>: <issue title>
298 | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
299 | Reason: <finding.reason>
300 | 
301 | Proposed change:
302 | <finding.suggestedValue>
303 | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
304 | Reply with:
305 |   apply     — accept and write to GitLab
306 |   edit <…>  — accept with your changes and write
307 |   skip      — move on without logging
308 |   reject    — discard and log rejection
309 | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
310 | ```
311 | 
312 | ### Decision handling
313 | 
314 | | User input | Action | Logged |
315 | |------------|--------|--------|
316 | | `apply` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: null })` | ✓ `accepted` |
317 | | `edit <text>` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: '<text>' })` | ✓ `edited` |
318 | | `skip` | No-op | ✗ not logged |
319 | | `reject` | Call `rejectFinding(finding)` | ✓ `rejected` |
320 | 
321 | **Only `apply` and `edit` call the GitLab writer adapter.** `skip` and `reject` do not
322 | modify any GitLab data.
323 | 
324 | ### Conflict Detection
325 | 
326 | A conflict arises when two agents produce suggestions that contradict each other on the same
327 | issue. The two most common cases:
328 | 
329 | - DEP suggests issue A *blocks* issue B (implying A must finish first), while ST suggests
330 |   transitioning A to Done (implying it is already complete).
331 | - AM rewrites a description in a way that would invalidate AC drafted by AC in the same run.
332 | 
333 | Before presenting the review, check for overlapping `issueIid` values across all agent
334 | findings. Conflicting findings are grouped and flagged:
335 | 
336 | ```
337 | ⚡ CONFLICT — Issue #7 has suggestions from two agents that may contradict:
338 | 
339 |   [ST] Proposed transition: Open → In Progress
340 |        (reason: MR !3 referencing this issue was opened 2h ago)
341 | 
342 |   [DEP] Proposed link: #7 blocks #9
343 |        (reason: both issues describe the same auth token refresh logic)
344 | 
345 |   → apply ST first / apply DEP first / apply both / skip both
346 | ```
347 | 
348 | Do not auto-resolve conflicts. The user decides.
349 | 
350 | When multiple agents produce findings for the **same issue IID** in the same session,
351 | surface them one at a time in a numbered list before presenting each individually:
352 | 
353 | ```
354 | ⚠️  Multiple findings for issue #<iid>:
355 |   1. [AC]  Draft missing acceptance criteria
356 |   2. [AM]  Rewrite vague description
357 | 
358 | Review them in order. Apply, edit, skip, or reject each separately.
359 | ```
360 | 
361 | After the user handles all findings for an issue, proceed to the next issue.
362 | 
363 | ### Writer adapter contract
364 | 
365 | At runtime, `applyFinding` calls the adapter only for **writable actions**.
366 | The `defaultWriterAdapter` (in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts`) deliberately returns
367 | `written: false` when no real adapter is injected, so telemetry will never record
368 | `outcome: accepted` for writes that never reached GitLab.  Pass `stubWriterAdapter`
369 | explicitly in unit tests.
370 | 
371 | Action-specific write semantics (for a real adapter):
372 | 
373 | | `action` | Write operation | Notes |
374 | |---|---|---|
375 | | `draft_ac` | Append drafted AC to issue description | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
376 | | `state_transition` | Apply scoped label swap; GitLab has only `opened`/`closed` states | `update-issue` |
377 | | `rewrite_desc` | Replace issue description with the drafted rewrite | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
378 | | `missing_coverage` | **Never written** — report only | COV findings are informational |
379 | | `dependency_link` | **Never written** by the adapter — report only | No links API; use `add-note` outside review loop if needed |
380 | 
381 | **Missing integration note:** The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool does not yet expose a
382 | native "add link" operation. Until it does, dependency links are presented as
383 | recommendations only.  The adapter boundary in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts` is the
384 | documented extension point for a future real integration.

393 | ### Logged events
394 | 
395 | One JSON object is appended per **accepted**, **edited**, or **rejected** decision.
396 | **Skip is neutral and NOT logged.**

398 | **Schema (one object per line):**

402 |   "agent": "AC",
403 |   "issueIid": 12,

406 |   "editedFields": []

409 | 
410 | **Security rules:**
411 | - Never log issue title, description, or any GitLab content.
412 | - Never log credentials, tokens, or URLs containing auth params.
413 | - The file is append-only; existing entries are never modified.
414 | - The file is gitignored (`sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl`).
415 | 
416 | ### Telemetry
417 | 
418 | Every apply / edit / reject outcome is appended to `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` in the
419 | repo root (append-only, never overwritten). The file is gitignored and contains no issue
420 | content — only metadata.
421 | 
422 | ```jsonc
423 | {
424 |   "ts": "2025-09-01T14:32:10Z",
425 |   "agent": "AC",
426 |   "issueIid": 12,
427 |   "action": "draft_ac",
428 |   "outcome": "accepted",   // "accepted" | "edited" | "rejected" | "failed"
429 |   "editedFields": []       // populated when outcome = "edited"
430 | }
431 | ```
432 | 
433 | The acceptance rate (`accepted / (accepted + rejected)`) is the primary trust metric for the demo.
434 | Note: `"failed"` outcomes (write attempted but adapter returned `written: false`) are excluded
435 | from both the numerator and denominator of all rate calculations.

439 | Call `computeAcceptanceRate(entries)` from `telemetry.ts` to get:

443 | Accepted:        N  (N%)
444 | Edited:          N  (N%)
445 | Rejected:        N  (N%)
446 | Failed:          N  (write did not reach GitLab — excluded from rates)
447 | Acceptance rate: N%     (accepted / total)
448 | Approval rate:   N%     (accepted + edited) / total
449 | ```

451 | Present this summary when the user asks "how are we doing?" or at the end of an Audit.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.

### Acceptance Criteria Agent (Task 20)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ac-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runAcAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`

The agent finds the issues that need criteria. **You write the criteria.** It returns a
`draft` brief, never finished prose — `suggestedValue` holds a placeholder, and
`applyFinding` throws if you try to apply a finding that still carries a brief.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Call `runAcAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
2. `null` means the issue already has usable criteria. Skip it silently.
3. Otherwise you get a finding with `draft: { task, context, unknowns }`:
   - Call `work-item-format` with `action: "get-template"` and
     `type: draft.context.workItemType`, and follow the structure it returns. That tool is
     the single source of truth for format — do not invent your own layout here.
   - Write 2–4 Given-When-Then criteria grounded in `draft.context.title` and
     `draft.context.description`. Cover the main path and at least one failure case.
   - If `draft.unknowns` is non-empty, those are gaps the issue does not fill. Put a
     direct question to the author in place of each gap. Do not choose a plausible value.
   - Replace `suggestedValue` with what you wrote, delete the `draft` field, then take the
     finding to Phase 4.

**Write criteria that could only belong to this issue.** Anything that would read the same
on an unrelated ticket is filler and should be rewritten — "the system responds correctly",
"the change takes effect and is visible in the UI", "no data is corrupted". If the issue
genuinely does not say enough to write a specific criterion, ask; a question is more useful
to the author than a sentence that asserts nothing.

**Detection rules (deterministic, no model needed):** returns `null` when the description
contains an "Acceptance Criteria" heading, `## AC`, `## Criteria`, or structured
Given/When/Then where each clause opens its own line. Three keywords in one line of prose
does not count.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues, `work-item-format` for the template.
Never call `gitlab-issue-writer` directly — writes go through the review interface.

### Ambiguity Detection Agent (Task 21)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ambiguity-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`

Same split as Task 20: the agent locates the vague wording, **you write the replacement.**
The finding carries a `draft` brief and a placeholder `suggestedValue`.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Call `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
2. `null` means the description is already specific. Do not flag it.
3. Otherwise:
   - `draft.context.flaggedPhrases` lists the exact spans that cannot be tested against.
     Replace each one. Leave the rest of the description alone.
   - `draft.context.reusableDetail` holds concrete material already in the issue — file
     paths, code references, error names. Prefer these over anything you supply yourself.
   - `draft.unknowns` lists flagged phrases with no replacement available in the issue.
     Write a question to the author in place of each. Never fill one with a guess.
   - Replace `suggestedValue` with the rewritten description, delete `draft`, then take the
     finding to Phase 4.

**This replaces the author's text, so keep their voice.** Rewrite what is vague and nothing
else. Do not expand a two-line bug report into a templated form with headings they did not
ask for, and do not add scope the author never mentioned. The result should read like the
same person wrote it on a better day.

Approving an AM finding **writes to the issue description**. That is deliberate — a rewrite
nobody can apply is not governance.

**False-positive avoidance:** returns `null` when a description is at least 80 characters
and carries two or more specificity signals (file paths, inline code, URLs, API/endpoint/
component/class/function references).

**Detected patterns:** placeholders (TBD/TODO/FIXME/XXX), non-specific pronouns
("the thing", "something", "somehow"), vague subjects ("fix it", "it doesn't work"),
non-testable claims ("does not work"), vague quantities ("various", "several things").
"properly" and "correctly" are deliberately absent — the AC agent's old template used them,
and flagging its output created a loop between the two agents.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues. Never writes directly.

### Dependency Suggestion Agent (Task 22)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/dependency-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runDependencyAgent(issues, config) → DependencyFinding[]`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Fetch all open issues via `gitlab-issue-reader` (action: `list-issues`, state: `opened`).
2. Call `runDependencyAgent(issues, projectConfig)`.
3. For each `DependencyFinding` returned:
   - Fields: `sourceIid`, `targetIid`, `suggestedLinkType` (`blocks` | `relates-to`),
     `reason`, `confidence` (0–1).
   - Proceed to Phase 4 for each finding.
4. Guarantees: no self-links, no duplicate pairs, confidence in [0,1].

**Overlap detection:** Jaccard similarity on significant keyword tokens (stop-words
removed). Threshold: 0.12 for a finding; 0.25 for high-confidence boost.

**Link type and direction:**
- `blocks` — only when exactly one side carries dependency language ("depends on",
  "requires", "prerequisite", "blocks"). The side that depends on the other is the
  target; the prerequisite side is the source.
- `relates-to` — when both or neither sides carry dependency language (direction is
  ambiguous). The lower IID is always set as `sourceIid` for canonical ordering.
- Domain-specific heuristics (e.g. matching "/token refresh/") are intentionally
  excluded from `BLOCKS_SIGNALS`; they produce unreliable directions on real backlogs.

**Report-only (no write path):** `DependencyFinding` objects are **always report-only**.
The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool has no native issue-links endpoint, so
`applyFinding` never writes for DEP findings (`gitlabWriteCalled` is always `false`).
Present the finding as a recommendation the team can action manually, or document it
as a comment by calling `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `add-note`) outside the normal
review loop if the user explicitly requests it.

### State Transition Agent (Task 23)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/state-transition-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, config) → AgentFinding | null`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. For each open issue, fetch related MRs via `gitlab-mr-reader-writer` (action: `list-mrs`).
   Match MRs by checking their `description` for `Closes #<iid>`, `Fixes #<iid>`, or the
   issue IID appearing in the MR title. Pass the matched MRs as the `mrs` parameter.
2. Call `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, projectConfig)`.
3. If the return value is `null`, skip — no transition warranted.
4. If the return value is an `AgentFinding` with `agent: 'ST'`:
   - The `suggestedValue` is the target state name (e.g. `'In Review'`).
   - Proceed to Phase 4.

**Signal mapping:**
- MR `state: 'merged'` → propose `'In Review'` (transitively reachable).
- MR `state: 'opened'` → propose `'In Progress'` (if valid from current state).
- No linked MRs → `null`.

**Transition validation:** Uses BFS over `config.transitionRules` to check transitive
reachability. A transition is only proposed if the target state is reachable from the
current state (directly or through intermediate states).

**NEVER automatically changes GitLab state.** All proposals go through Phase 4.

**Write path (if user accepts):** Call `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `update-issue`)
with the appropriate `state_event` (`close` for Done, otherwise update labels to reflect
the new state).

## Phase 4 — Human Review Interface (Task 25)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/review.ts`
**Exports:** `applyFinding(finding, options, adapter?)`, `rejectFinding(finding)`

### Review presentation

For each `AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding`, present to the user:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔍 [AGENT-TAG] Issue #<iid>: <issue title>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reason: <finding.reason>

Proposed change:
<finding.suggestedValue>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reply with:
  apply     — accept and write to GitLab
  edit <…>  — accept with your changes and write
  skip      — move on without logging
  reject    — discard and log rejection
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

### Decision handling

| User input | Action | Logged |
|------------|--------|--------|
| `apply` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: null })` | ✓ `accepted` |
| `edit <text>` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: '<text>' })` | ✓ `edited` |
| `skip` | No-op | ✗ not logged |
| `reject` | Call `rejectFinding(finding)` | ✓ `rejected` |

**Only `apply` and `edit` call the GitLab writer adapter.** `skip` and `reject` do not
modify any GitLab data.

### Conflict Detection

A conflict arises when two agents produce suggestions that contradict each other on the same
issue. The two most common cases:

- DEP suggests issue A *blocks* issue B (implying A must finish first), while ST suggests
  transitioning A to Done (implying it is already complete).
- AM rewrites a description in a way that would invalidate AC drafted by AC in the same run.

Before presenting the review, check for overlapping `issueIid` values across all agent
findings. Conflicting findings are grouped and flagged:

```
⚡ CONFLICT — Issue #7 has suggestions from two agents that may contradict:

  [ST] Proposed transition: Open → In Progress
       (reason: MR !3 referencing this issue was opened 2h ago)

  [DEP] Proposed link: #7 blocks #9
       (reason: both issues describe the same auth token refresh logic)

  → apply ST first / apply DEP first / apply both / skip both
```

Do not auto-resolve conflicts. The user decides.

When multiple agents produce findings for the **same issue IID** in the same session,
surface them one at a time in a numbered list before presenting each individually:

```
⚠️  Multiple findings for issue #<iid>:
  1. [AC]  Draft missing acceptance criteria
  2. [AM]  Rewrite vague description

Review them in order. Apply, edit, skip, or reject each separately.
```

After the user handles all findings for an issue, proceed to the next issue.

### Writer adapter contract

At runtime, `applyFinding` calls the adapter only for **writable actions**.
The `defaultWriterAdapter` (in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts`) deliberately returns
`written: false` when no real adapter is injected, so telemetry will never record
`outcome: accepted` for writes that never reached GitLab.  Pass `stubWriterAdapter`
explicitly in unit tests.

Action-specific write semantics (for a real adapter):

| `action` | Write operation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `draft_ac` | Append drafted AC to issue description | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `state_transition` | Apply scoped label swap; GitLab has only `opened`/`closed` states | `update-issue` |
| `rewrite_desc` | Replace issue description with the drafted rewrite | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `missing_coverage` | **Never written** — report only | COV findings are informational |
| `dependency_link` | **Never written** by the adapter — report only | No links API; use `add-note` outside review loop if needed |

**Missing integration note:** The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool does not yet expose a
native "add link" operation. Until it does, dependency links are presented as
recommendations only.  The adapter boundary in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts` is the
documented extension point for a future real integration.

## Phase 5 — Suggestion Telemetry (Task 26)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/telemetry.ts`
**File:** `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` (in the working directory; gitignored)

### Logged events

One JSON object is appended per **accepted**, **edited**, or **rejected** decision.
**Skip is neutral and NOT logged.**

**Schema (one object per line):**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-09-01T10:00:00.000Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",
  "editedFields": []
}
```

**Security rules:**
- Never log issue title, description, or any GitLab content.
- Never log credentials, tokens, or URLs containing auth params.
- The file is append-only; existing entries are never modified.
- The file is gitignored (`sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl`).

### Telemetry

Every apply / edit / reject outcome is appended to `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` in the
repo root (append-only, never overwritten). The file is gitignored and contains no issue
content — only metadata.

```jsonc
{
  "ts": "2025-09-01T14:32:10Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",   // "accepted" | "edited" | "rejected" | "failed"
  "editedFields": []       // populated when outcome = "edited"
}
```

The acceptance rate (`accepted / (accepted + rejected)`) is the primary trust metric for the demo.
Note: `"failed"` outcomes (write attempted but adapter returned `written: false`) are excluded
from both the numerator and denominator of all rate calculations.

### Acceptance-rate summary

Call `computeAcceptanceRate(entries)` from `telemetry.ts` to get:

```
Total:           N decisions logged (failed excluded)
Accepted:        N  (N%)
Edited:          N  (N%)
Rejected:        N  (N%)
Failed:          N  (write did not reach GitLab — excluded from rates)
Acceptance rate: N%     (accepted / total)
Approval rate:   N%     (accepted + edited) / total
```

Present this summary when the user asks "how are we doing?" or at the end of an Audit.

### Environment override

Set `SDLC_TELEMETRY_PATH` env var to redirect the telemetry file (used in tests).

to the author than a sentence that asserts nothing.

**Detection rules (deterministic, no model needed):** returns `null` when the description
contains an "Acceptance Criteria" heading, `## AC`, `## Criteria`, or structured
Given/When/Then where each clause opens its own line. Three keywords in one line of prose
does not count.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues, `work-item-format` for the template.
Never call `gitlab-issue-writer` directly — writes go through the review interface.

---

### Ambiguity Detection Agent (Task 21)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ambiguity-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`

Same split as Task 20: the agent locates the vague wording, **you write the replacement.**
The finding carries a `draft` brief and a placeholder `suggestedValue`.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Call `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
2. `null` means the description is already specific. Do not flag it.
3. Otherwise:
   - `draft.context.flaggedPhrases` lists the exact spans that cannot be tested against.
     Replace each one. Leave the rest of the description alone.
   - `draft.context.reusableDetail` holds concrete material already in the issue — file
     paths, code references, error names. Prefer these over anything you supply yourself.
   - `draft.unknowns` lists flagged phrases with no replacement available in the issue.
     Write a question to the author in place of each. Never fill one with a guess.
   - Replace `suggestedValue` with the rewritten description, delete `draft`, then take the
     finding to Phase 4.

**This replaces the author's text, so keep their voice.** Rewrite what is vague and nothing
else. Do not expand a two-line bug report into a templated form with headings they did not
ask for, and do not add scope the author never mentioned. The result should read like the
same person wrote it on a better day.

Approving an AM finding **writes to the issue description**. That is deliberate — a rewrite
nobody can apply is not governance.

**False-positive avoidance:** returns `null` when a description is at least 80 characters
and carries two or more specificity signals (file paths, inline code, URLs, API/endpoint/
component/class/function references).

**Detected patterns:** placeholders (TBD/TODO/FIXME/XXX), non-specific pronouns
("the thing", "something", "somehow"), vague subjects ("fix it", "it doesn't work"),
non-testable claims ("does not work"), vague quantities ("various", "several things").
"properly" and "correctly" are deliberately absent — the AC agent's old template used them,
and flagging its output created a loop between the two agents.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues. Never writes directly.

---

### Dependency Suggestion Agent (Task 22)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/dependency-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runDependencyAgent(issues, config) → DependencyFinding[]`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Fetch all open issues via `gitlab-issue-reader` (action: `list-issues`, state: `opened`).
2. Call `runDependencyAgent(issues, projectConfig)`.
3. For each `DependencyFinding` returned:
   - Fields: `sourceIid`, `targetIid`, `suggestedLinkType` (`blocks` | `relates-to`),
     `reason`, `confidence` (0–1).
   - Proceed to Phase 4 for each finding.
4. Guarantees: no self-links, no duplicate pairs, confidence in [0,1].

**Overlap detection:** Jaccard similarity on significant keyword tokens (stop-words
removed). Threshold: 0.12 for a finding; 0.25 for high-confidence boost.

**Link type and direction:**
- `blocks` — only when exactly one side carries dependency language ("depends on",
  "requires", "prerequisite", "blocks"). The side that depends on the other is the
  target; the prerequisite side is the source.
- `relates-to` — when both or neither sides carry dependency language (direction is
  ambiguous). The lower IID is always set as `sourceIid` for canonical ordering.
- Domain-specific heuristics (e.g. matching "/token refresh/") are intentionally
  excluded from `BLOCKS_SIGNALS`; they produce unreliable directions on real backlogs.

**Report-only (no write path):** `DependencyFinding` objects are **always report-only**.
The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool has no native issue-links endpoint, so
`applyFinding` never writes for DEP findings (`gitlabWriteCalled` is always `false`).
Present the finding as a recommendation the team can action manually, or document it
as a comment by calling `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `add-note`) outside the normal
review loop if the user explicitly requests it.

---

### State Transition Agent (Task 23)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/state-transition-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, config) → AgentFinding | null`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. For each open issue, fetch related MRs via `gitlab-mr-reader-writer` (action: `list-mrs`).
   Match MRs by checking their `description` for `Closes #<iid>`, `Fixes #<iid>`, or the
   issue IID appearing in the MR title. Pass the matched MRs as the `mrs` parameter.
2. Call `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, projectConfig)`.
3. If the return value is `null`, skip — no transition warranted.
4. If the return value is an `AgentFinding` with `agent: 'ST'`:
   - The `suggestedValue` is the target state name (e.g. `'In Review'`).
   - Proceed to Phase 4.

**Signal mapping:**
- MR `state: 'merged'` → propose `'In Review'` (transitively reachable).
- MR `state: 'opened'` → propose `'In Progress'` (if valid from current state).
- No linked MRs → `null`.

**Transition validation:** Uses BFS over `config.transitionRules` to check transitive
reachability. A transition is only proposed if the target state is reachable from the
current state (directly or through intermediate states).

**NEVER automatically changes GitLab state.** All proposals go through Phase 4.

**Write path (if user accepts):** Call `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `update-issue`)
with the appropriate `state_event` (`close` for Done, otherwise update labels to reflect
the new state).

---

### Test Coverage Linkage Agent (Task 24 — P1 stretch, disabled by default)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/coverage-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runCoverageAgent(issues, testContents, config) → AgentFinding[]`

**Enabled only when** `config.coverage.enabled === true` in the project config.
Add `"coverage": { "testFilePatterns": ["**/*.test.ts"], "enabled": true }` to
`.sdlc-harness.json` to enable.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Read test file contents matching the configured glob patterns.
2. Call `runCoverageAgent(issues, testContents, projectConfig)`.
3. Issues with no `#<iid>` or `closes #<iid>` reference in any test file are flagged.
4. Surface each finding through Phase 4.

## Phase 4 — Human Review Interface (Task 25)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/review.ts`
**Exports:** `applyFinding(finding, options, adapter?)`, `rejectFinding(finding)`

### Review presentation

For each `AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding`, present to the user:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔍 [AGENT-TAG] Issue #<iid>: <issue title>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reason: <finding.reason>

Proposed change:
<finding.suggestedValue>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reply with:
  apply     — accept and write to GitLab
  edit <…>  — accept with your changes and write
  skip      — move on without logging
  reject    — discard and log rejection
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

### Decision handling

| User input | Action | Logged |
|------------|--------|--------|
| `apply` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: null })` | ✓ `accepted` |
| `edit <text>` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: '<text>' })` | ✓ `edited` |
| `skip` | No-op | ✗ not logged |
| `reject` | Call `rejectFinding(finding)` | ✓ `rejected` |

**Only `apply` and `edit` call the GitLab writer adapter.** `skip` and `reject` do not
modify any GitLab data.

### Conflict Detection

A conflict arises when two agents produce suggestions that contradict each other on the same
issue. The two most common cases:

- DEP suggests issue A *blocks* issue B (implying A must finish first), while ST suggests
  transitioning A to Done (implying it is already complete).
- AM rewrites a description in a way that would invalidate AC drafted by AC in the same run.

Before presenting the review, check for overlapping `issueIid` values across all agent
findings. Conflicting findings are grouped and flagged:

```
⚡ CONFLICT — Issue #7 has suggestions from two agents that may contradict:

  [ST] Proposed transition: Open → In Progress
       (reason: MR !3 referencing this issue was opened 2h ago)

  [DEP] Proposed link: #7 blocks #9
       (reason: both issues describe the same auth token refresh logic)

  → apply ST first / apply DEP first / apply both / skip both
```

Do not auto-resolve conflicts. The user decides.

When multiple agents produce findings for the **same issue IID** in the same session,
surface them one at a time in a numbered list before presenting each individually:

```
⚠️  Multiple findings for issue #<iid>:
  1. [AC]  Draft missing acceptance criteria
  2. [AM]  Rewrite vague description

Review them in order. Apply, edit, skip, or reject each separately.
```

After the user handles all findings for an issue, proceed to the next issue.

### Writer adapter contract

At runtime, `applyFinding` calls the adapter only for **writable actions**.
The `defaultWriterAdapter` (in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts`) deliberately returns
`written: false` when no real adapter is injected, so telemetry will never record
`outcome: accepted` for writes that never reached GitLab.  Pass `stubWriterAdapter`
explicitly in unit tests.

Action-specific write semantics (for a real adapter):

| `action` | Write operation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `draft_ac` | Append drafted AC to issue description | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `state_transition` | Apply scoped label swap; GitLab has only `opened`/`closed` states | `update-issue` |
| `rewrite_desc` | Replace issue description with the drafted rewrite | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `missing_coverage` | **Never written** — report only | COV findings are informational |
| `dependency_link` | **Never written** by the adapter — report only | No links API; use `add-note` outside review loop if needed |

**Missing integration note:** The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool does not yet expose a
native "add link" operation. Until it does, dependency links are presented as
recommendations only.  The adapter boundary in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts` is the
documented extension point for a future real integration.

## Phase 5 — Suggestion Telemetry (Task 26)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/telemetry.ts`
**File:** `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` (in the working directory; gitignored)

### Logged events

One JSON object is appended per **accepted**, **edited**, or **rejected** decision.
**Skip is neutral and NOT logged.**

**Schema (one object per line):**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-09-01T10:00:00.000Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",
  "editedFields": []
}
```

**Security rules:**
- Never log issue title, description, or any GitLab content.
- Never log credentials, tokens, or URLs containing auth params.
- The file is append-only; existing entries are never modified.
- The file is gitignored (`sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl`).

### Telemetry

Every apply / edit / reject outcome is appended to `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` in the
repo root (append-only, never overwritten). The file is gitignored and contains no issue
content — only metadata.

```jsonc
{
  "ts": "2025-09-01T14:32:10Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",   // "accepted" | "edited" | "rejected" | "failed"
  "editedFields": []       // populated when outcome = "edited"
}
```

The acceptance rate (`accepted / (accepted + rejected)`) is the primary trust metric for the demo.
Note: `"failed"` outcomes (write attempted but adapter returned `written: false`) are excluded
from both the numerator and denominator of all rate calculations.

### Acceptance-rate summary

Call `computeAcceptanceRate(entries)` from `telemetry.ts` to get:

```
Total:           N decisions logged (failed excluded)
Accepted:        N  (N%)
Edited:          N  (N%)
Rejected:        N  (N%)
Failed:          N  (write did not reach GitLab — excluded from rates)
Acceptance rate: N%     (accepted / total)
Approval rate:   N%     (accepted + edited) / total
```

Present this summary when the user asks "how are we doing?" or at the end of an Audit.

### Environment override

Set `SDLC_TELEMETRY_PATH` env var to redirect the telemetry file (used in tests).

# AGENTS.md — Agent (coding) mode

This file provides guidance to agents when working with code in this repository.

- **`app.js` script tag is at the bottom of `<body>` — not deferred.** DOM elements are guaranteed present when the script runs; do not add `DOMContentLoaded` guards.

# Project Instructions (AGENTS.md)

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to agents when working with code in this repository.

## Repository Layout

| Directory | What it is |
|---|---|
| `gitlab-local/` | Docker stack — GitLab CE + nginx demo site. All manage scripts live here. |
| `weather-app/` | The demo artefact (plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step). Served by nginx on port 8081. |
| `bob-kit/` | Bob config **templates only** — must be manually merged/installed, not used in-place. |
| `docs/` | Plans and session notes. |
| `bob-sessions/` | Bob task-session exports — committed to repo for hackathon submission, not ignored. |

## Stack

- **GitLab** runs via Docker Compose (`gitlab/gitlab-ce:latest`) on port 8080.
- **Demo site** is `weather-app/` mounted read-only into `nginx:alpine` on port 8081.
- **No Node/npm/Python build** anywhere in the repo — the weather app is plain files opened directly in a browser.
- **GitLab MCP server** uses the official `mcp/gitlab` Docker image run via `docker run --network host` (not a local process).

## Key Commands

```bash
# Start the full stack (first boot takes 3–5 minutes)
cd gitlab-local && docker compose up -d

# Validate stack health (polls until HTTP 200/302 or 300 s timeout)
./gitlab-local/smoke.sh

# Seed / reset demo data (idempotent — safe to re-run)
./gitlab-local/manage.sh seed

# Full wipe and reseed (clean demo state)
cd gitlab-local && docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d && ./manage.sh seed

# Other manage.sh sub-commands: start | stop | restart | logs | status | password
./gitlab-local/manage.sh status
```

## Critical Gotchas

- **`.env` is gitignored and bobignored.** Copy `gitlab-local/.env.example` → `gitlab-local/.env` and set `GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD`. The seed script reads this file; it will hard-fail with no fallback if the variable is absent.
- **Same password for root and demo user.** `seed.sh` sets both the `root` admin and the `demo` developer account to `$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
- **`seed.sh` must be run from inside the `sdlc-harness` repo.** It resolves `../weather-app` relative to its own directory — running it from an arbitrary path will fail.
- **`seed.sh` creates an ephemeral API token** via `gitlab-rails runner` and writes it to `/tmp/seed_token.txt` inside the container, then deletes it. Do not store or reuse this token.
- **Weather app mock data is deterministic.** `hashString(city.toLowerCase().trim())` seeds all values — the same city always returns the same numbers. Do not expect random variation.
- **Theme key in localStorage is `sdlc-theme`** (not `theme` or app name). Use this key if writing tests against localStorage state.
- **`bob-kit/` is a template, not a live config.** Files there must be manually merged into `~/.bob/settings/custom_modes.yaml`, `~/.bob/skills/`, and the Bob global MCP config. They are not auto-loaded.
- **`.sdlc-harness.json`** is written to the repo root by the skill's onboarding phase (Phase 1). Check for this file to determine if a project has been onboarded.
- **MCP server scope is locked to the onboarded project.** The skill must not read/write issues outside the project configured in `.sdlc-harness.json`, even when scanning for dependency links.
- **`bob-sessions/` is committed** — the `.gitignore` explicitly excludes live AI session state (`.copilot/`, `.cursor/`) but the `bob-sessions/` export folder must be committed for hackathon submission.

## Bob Kit Installation (one-time, per machine)

```bash
cp -r bob-kit/rules/. .bob/rules/              # workspace rules
cp -r bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness ~/.bob/skills/  # global skill
# MCP: merge bob-kit/mcp/mcp.json into Bob IDE → Settings → MCP → Edit Global MCP
# Modes: merge bob-kit/custom_modes.yaml into ~/.bob/settings/custom_modes.yaml
```

## Weather App — Coding Conventions

- All JS is vanilla ES5-compatible (no modules, no bundler). `app.js` is placed at the bottom of `<body>` — it is **not** deferred or async.
- JSDoc comments on every exported function with `@param` and `@returns` types.
- DOM references are declared as module-level `const` after the data/utility block (section 2 of `app.js`).
- CSS theming uses `data-theme` attribute on `<body>` (`light`|`dark`), driven by `applyTheme()`.
- Section separators in `app.js` use a fixed-width `/* ---… */` banner with a section number and title.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultrathink this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

The `/tmp/runner.rb` approach works — GitLab created the token. Now I have all the evidence needed:

---

## Root Cause Analysis

There are **two distinct bugs** that each independently break `./manage.sh seed`:

---

### Bug 1 — `bash` resolves to WSL `bash.exe` in PowerShell (the main blocker)

When you run `.\manage.sh seed` from a PowerShell terminal, `manage.sh` calls `bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/seed.sh"`. But `bash` in PowerShell resolves to `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` — which is **WSL**. WSL's Docker context is not integrated with Docker Desktop, so every `docker exec` command inside `seed.sh` fails with:

```
The command 'docker' could not be found in this WSL 2 distro.
```

The fix: run the script using **Git Bash** (`"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe"`), which uses the Windows Docker context where `docker` works correctly.

---

### Bug 2 — `gitlab-rails runner` receives a truncated/broken inline script on Windows

Even inside Git Bash, the `docker exec gitlab gitlab-rails runner "..."` multiline string in [`seed.sh:47-59`](gitlab-local/seed.sh:47) is mangled on Windows because of how shell quoting and line endings interact when the script is launched from a Windows host shell. The token file ends up empty, triggering the `ERROR: Could not create API token` guard at line 64.

The fix in `seed.sh` is to write the Ruby script to a temp file inside the container first, then run it — which bypasses the quoting issue entirely.

---

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# seed.sh — Idempotent demo seed for the local GitLab instance.

set -euo pipefail

# Load .env if present and GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not already set
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ] && [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  set -a; source "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"; set +a
fi

if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not set."
  echo "  Copy gitlab-local/.env.example to gitlab-local/.env and set the variable."
  exit 1
fi

ROOT_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"
DEMO_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"

echo "Waiting for GitLab to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$GITLAB_URL/users/sign_in" 2>&1)
  if [ "$status" = "200" ]; then
    echo "GitLab is ready."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/40] HTTP $status — retrying in 15s..."
  sleep 15
  if [ "$i" -eq 40 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: GitLab did not become ready in time. Is the container running?"
    exit 1
  fi

  begin
    PersonalAccessToken.where(name: 'seed-script-token', user_id: 1).delete_all
    token = User.find(1).personal_access_tokens.create!(
      name: 'seed-script-token',
      scopes: [:api],
      expires_at: Date.today + 365
    )

    File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', 'ERROR: ' + e.message)

  local commit_msg="$3"

  encoded_path=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote('$file_path', safe=''))")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# seed.sh — Idempotent demo seed for the local GitLab instance.
# Creates a demo group, demo user, and the Weather Dashboard demo project
# sourced from the sdlc-harness dev branch.
# Safe to run multiple times — skips anything that already exists.
#
# Reads GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD from the environment or from .env in the
# same directory as this script. Never falls back to a hardcoded value.
set -euo pipefail

# Load .env if present and GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not already set
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ] && [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  set -a; source "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"; set +a
fi

if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not set."
  echo "  Copy gitlab-local/.env.example to gitlab-local/.env and set the variable."
  exit 1
fi

GITLAB_URL="http://localhost:8080"
ROOT_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"
DEMO_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"

# ── Wait for GitLab to be ready ──────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "Waiting for GitLab to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$GITLAB_URL/users/sign_in" 2>&1)
  if [ "$status" = "200" ]; then
    echo "GitLab is ready."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/40] HTTP $status — retrying in 15s..."
  sleep 15
  if [ "$i" -eq 40 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: GitLab did not become ready in time. Is the container running?"
    exit 1
  fi
done

# ── Create a root API token via Rails runner (write to file inside container) -
echo ""
echo "Creating API token for root..."
# Write the Ruby script to a temp file inside the container to avoid shell
# quoting/line-ending issues when running from a Windows host (Git Bash).
docker exec gitlab bash -c 'cat > /tmp/runner.rb' <<'RUBY'
begin
  PersonalAccessToken.where(name: 'seed-script-token', user_id: 1).delete_all
  token = User.find(1).personal_access_tokens.create!(
    name: 'seed-script-token',
    scopes: [:api],
    expires_at: Date.today + 365
  )
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', token.token)
rescue => e
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', 'ERROR: ' + e.message)
end
RUBY
docker exec gitlab gitlab-rails runner /tmp/runner.rb 2>/dev/null
docker exec gitlab rm -f /tmp/runner.rb 2>/dev/null || true

TOKEN=$(docker exec gitlab cat /tmp/seed_token.txt 2>/dev/null || true)
docker exec gitlab rm -f /tmp/seed_token.txt 2>/dev/null || true

if [ -z "$TOKEN" ] || [[ "$TOKEN" == ERROR:* ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: Could not create API token: $TOKEN"
  echo "  Make sure GitLab is fully started and try again."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Token obtained."

# ── Helper: call GitLab API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
api() {
  local method="$1"; local path="$2"; shift 2
  curl -sf -X "$method" \
    -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# seed.sh — Idempotent demo seed for the local GitLab instance.

  set -a; source "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"; set +a
fi

  echo "ERROR: GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not set."
  echo "  Copy gitlab-local/.env.example to gitlab-local/.env and set the variable."
  exit 1

GITLAB_URL="http://localhost:8080"
ROOT_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"
DEMO_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"

trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT

# ── Wait for GitLab to be ready ──────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "Waiting for GitLab to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$GITLAB_URL/users/sign_in" 2>&1)
  if [ "$status" = "200" ]; then
    echo "GitLab is ready."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/40] HTTP $status — retrying in 15s..."
  sleep 15
  if [ "$i" -eq 40 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: GitLab did not become ready in time. Is the container running?"
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "Creating API token for root..."
# Write the Ruby script to a local temp file then docker-cp it into the
# container. This avoids shell quoting / line-ending issues when the script
# is invoked from a Windows host (Git Bash or similar).
RUNNER_TMP="$TMP_DIR/runner.rb"
cat > "$RUNNER_TMP" <<'RUBY'
begin
  PersonalAccessToken.where(name: 'seed-script-token', user_id: 1).delete_all
  token = User.find(1).personal_access_tokens.create!(
    name: 'seed-script-token',
    scopes: [:api],
    expires_at: Date.today + 365
  )
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', token.token)
rescue => e
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', 'ERROR: ' + e.message)
end

    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    "$GITLAB_URL/api/v4/$path" "$@"
}

  echo "  Created group 'SDLC Harness' (id=$GROUP_ID)"

import sys, json

" 2>/dev/null)

  USER_ID=$(api POST "users" -d "{

  echo "  Created user 'demo' (id=$USER_ID)"
else

  echo "  Added 'demo' to group as Developer"

echo ""
echo "Adding project files..."

add_file() {
  local file_path="$1"
  local src_file="$2"

  encoded_path=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote('$file_path', safe=''))")

  exists=$(api GET "projects/$PROJECT_ID/repository/files/${encoded_path}?ref=main" 2>/dev/null \

There's the bug. Git Bash expands `/tmp/runner.rb` to a Windows path (`C:/Users/matgo/AppData/Local/Temp/runner.rb`) when it's passed as an argument to a command. The container path `/tmp/runner.rb` inside the `docker exec` command is being POSIX-path-converted by Git Bash's path translation.

The fix: quote the path so Git Bash doesn't translate it, or use a different approach to pass the script. The cleanest solution is to pass the Ruby code via stdin using `-` as the filename for `gitlab-rails runner`:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# seed.sh — Idempotent demo seed for the local GitLab instance.

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ] && [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  set -a; source "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"; set +a
fi

if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not set."
  echo "  Copy gitlab-local/.env.example to gitlab-local/.env and set the variable."
  exit 1
fi

GITLAB_URL="http://localhost:8080"
ROOT_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"
DEMO_PASSWORD="$GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD"

TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT

# ── Wait for GitLab to be ready ──────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "Waiting for GitLab to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$GITLAB_URL/users/sign_in" 2>&1)
  if [ "$status" = "200" ]; then
    echo "GitLab is ready."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/40] HTTP $status — retrying in 15s..."
  sleep 15
  if [ "$i" -eq 40 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: GitLab did not become ready in time. Is the container running?"
    exit 1
  fi
done

# ── Create a root API token via Rails runner (write to file inside container) -

echo "Creating API token for root..."
# Write the Ruby script to a local temp file then docker-cp it into the
# container. This avoids shell quoting / line-ending issues when the script
# is invoked from a Windows host (Git Bash or similar).

begin
  PersonalAccessToken.where(name: 'seed-script-token', user_id: 1).delete_all
  token = User.find(1).personal_access_tokens.create!(
    name: 'seed-script-token',
    scopes: [:api],
    expires_at: Date.today + 365
  )
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', token.token)
rescue => e
  File.write('/tmp/seed_token.txt', 'ERROR: ' + e.message)
end

add_file() {

  local src_file="$2"

  encoded_path=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote('$file_path', safe=''))")

if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ] && [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  set -a; source "$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"; set +a
fi

if [ -z "${GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD is not set."
  echo "  Copy gitlab-local/.env.example to gitlab-local/.env and set the variable."

data.content:
**Found it.** `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` prevents Git Bash from translating `/dev/null` to the Windows null device, causing `curl -o /dev/null` to fail (it tries to write a file named literally `/dev/null` which doesn't exist as a Windows path). Using `NUL` instead works.

The fix: in `seed.sh`, change all `curl -o /dev/null` to `curl -o NUL` when running on Windows with Git Bash, **or** better yet — don't use `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` globally, since it breaks `/dev/null`. Instead, only suppress path conversion for the specific `docker exec` commands that need it, using the per-command `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker exec ...` prefix.
